stories.title: Judgment on Edom
stories.keyVerse: "Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the LORD."
stories.retelling:
In the heat of the desert sun, the rocky strongholds of Edom stood proud and unyielding, carved into the sheer faces of the mountains. The people of Edom, confident in their towering fortresses, believed themselves invincible. They had grown arrogant, their hearts hardened with pride, like eagles perched in lofty nests, daring anyone to challenge their dominion.

But a shadow loomed over Edom, a whisper of impending doom carried on the wind. The vision came to Obadiah, a message from the Lord: Edom, once revered and feared, would be diminished, despised among the nations. Their pride—rooted in their seemingly impregnable homes among the cliffs—had blinded them to their vulnerability.

An ambassador moved among the nations, rallying them against Edom. **“Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle,”** the call to arms echoed. The nations, once allies, turned against Edom, their former trust now a weapon used to deceive and ensnare them. Those who once shared bread with Edom had set a trap, and understanding fled from the deceived.

The Lord declared, through Obadiah, that Edom's downfall was inevitable. **“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars,”** the message rang, **“thence will I bring thee down.”** The proud heights from which they mocked their enemies would become their undoing.

Edom's betrayal against their kin, the descendants of Jacob, was a stain upon their history. In a moment of vulnerability, when foreign invaders breached the gates of Jerusalem, Edom had stood aside, indifferent, and even joined in the plunder. They had gloated over Judah's misfortune, celebrating their downfall as if it were a spectacle for their amusement.

Now, the day of reckoning approached. The Lord's judgment was swift and uncompromising. Edom, having once rejoiced over Judah's calamity, would find their deeds returned upon their own heads. Their hidden treasures would be exposed, their mighty warriors dismayed, and their wise men silenced.

From the south, the people of Israel would rise, reclaiming lands and possessions. The house of Jacob and Joseph would become a consuming fire, while Edom, like dry stubble, would be reduced to ashes. The lands they once occupied would be possessed by others: the mount of Esau, the plains of the Philistines, and beyond.

As the vision unfolded, it became clear that Edom's time was over. The kingdom would belong to the Lord, and saviors would ascend Mount Zion to judge Edom's mountains. The proud would be humbled, and those who once dwelled in the heights would face the stark reality of their fall. In this new order, justice would reign, and the Lord's sovereignty would be unchallenged.
